control: Leadership approves the security program, its owner, and its budget, and reviews progress at least twice a year.
evidence: Meeting notes or minutes with attendees, date, and decisions

control: A named security owner has written responsibilities and the time to carry them out.
evidence: Role description or org chart naming the owner; leadership sign-off

control: Security policies are written, approved, published where staff can find them, and reviewed each year.
evidence: Policy set with version, approver, and approval date; review record

control: Everyone acknowledges the code of conduct and key policies at hire and each year.
evidence: Acknowledgment records from the HR or e-signature tool

control: Customer commitments (security terms, SLAs, and the system description) are kept current and shared with customers.
evidence: Published trust page or contract template; dated system description

control: A risk assessment covering security, fraud, and major changes is done each year and when the business changes.
evidence: Risk register with likelihood, impact, owner, treatment, and review date

control: Each high risk has an owner and a treatment plan that leadership has accepted.
evidence: Register entries with treatment, owner, and acceptance sign-off

control: An inventory of systems, data stores, and the data each holds is kept current.
evidence: System and data inventory with owner and data classification

control: An independent check of the controls (internal review or outside readiness assessment) happens each year.
evidence: Review report and the tracked fixes

control: New hires are background checked where the law allows, before they get access to customer data.
evidence: Check completion record for each hire in the period

control: Staff and contractors sign confidentiality terms before access.
evidence: Signed agreements for each hire and contractor

control: Everyone completes security awareness training at hire and each year.
evidence: Training completion report with names and dates

control: Performance and conduct issues, including security policy breaches, follow a written process.
evidence: Disciplinary policy; anonymized case log if any occurred

control: Access is granted by role, approved by the system owner, and recorded in a ticket.
evidence: Access request tickets with approver and date, sampled across the period

control: Departing staff lose access to every system within one business day.
evidence: Departure list matched to account disable times

control: System owners review who has access each quarter and fix what they find.
evidence: Signed review with the user list, the changes made, and dates

control: Single sign-on and phishing-resistant two-step sign-in are required for company systems.
evidence: SSO and MFA policy settings; report of users and MFA status

control: Administrator and production access is limited to named people, uses separate accounts, and is logged.
evidence: Admin list; access logs; review record

control: Service accounts and keys have owners, are stored in a secrets manager, and are rotated.
evidence: Secrets inventory with owners and last rotation dates

control: Company laptops and phones are managed, encrypted, screen locked, and kept up to date.
evidence: Device management compliance report

control: Office and equipment areas are locked, and visitors are signed in; data center security is inherited from the cloud provider.
evidence: Office access list; visitor log; cloud provider SOC report

control: Lost or stolen devices are reported and wiped, and retired devices are wiped with a record.
evidence: Device log with wipe confirmations

control: Production networks restrict inbound traffic to what is needed, and changes go through review.
evidence: Firewall or security group rules; change tickets

control: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest with managed keys.
evidence: TLS configuration; storage and database encryption settings

control: Systems and dependencies are scanned for vulnerabilities, and findings are fixed within set timeframes.
evidence: Scan reports; tickets showing fix dates against the policy timeframes

control: An outside penetration test runs each year and its findings are tracked to closure.
evidence: Test report; remediation tickets

control: Code and infrastructure changes are reviewed by someone other than the author before production.
evidence: Pull requests with an approving reviewer, sampled across the period

control: Changes pass automated tests and deploy through a pipeline; no one edits production by hand.
evidence: Pipeline configuration; branch protection settings; deploy logs

control: Development, test, and production are separate, and production data is not used in testing.
evidence: Account or environment layout; data handling rule

control: Emergency changes are allowed, recorded, and reviewed after the fact.
evidence: Emergency change log with after-the-fact approvals

control: Logs from production and identity systems are collected, kept for a set time, and protected from change.
evidence: Log settings with retention; access restrictions

control: Alerts for security events and outages reach an on-call person, who responds.
evidence: Alert rules; on-call schedule; sample alert with response

control: Capacity and performance are monitored against thresholds.
evidence: Dashboards and alert thresholds

control: A written incident response plan names roles, severity levels, and contact steps, including customer notice.
evidence: Approved plan with review date

control: Incidents are logged, handled per the plan, and closed with lessons learned.
evidence: Incident tickets with timeline, actions, and a review

control: The incident plan is exercised with a tabletop each year.
evidence: Tabletop notes with attendees, scenario, and follow-ups

control: Backups run on schedule, are encrypted, and are stored apart from production.
evidence: Backup settings and job history

control: A restore from backup is tested at least each year, with the time it took recorded.
evidence: Restore test record with date, data restored, and duration

control: A continuity plan covers loss of a key system, provider, or person, and is reviewed each year.
evidence: Approved plan; review record

control: Vendors that touch customer data are reviewed before signing and each year, by risk.
evidence: Vendor list with risk tier; review records; SOC reports collected

control: Contracts with key vendors include security and confidentiality terms.
evidence: Contracts or DPAs with security clauses

control: Customer responsibilities from vendor SOC reports (complementary user entity controls) are met.
evidence: Vendor CUEC list mapped to the company's own controls

control: Data is classified, and confidential data is handled per its class.
evidence: Classification policy; inventory showing classes

control: Customer data is deleted on request or at contract end, within a set time, with a record.
evidence: Deletion requests with completion dates
